# Investigation: `Context.res` setter — response header merging (esp. `Set-Cookie`)

Read-only investigation of Hono `4.13.18` (`package.json:3`). No source or test files were modified.
All references are to the repository root.

---

## 1. Summary

`Context.res`'s setter (`src/context.ts:414-434`) is **not** a plain assignment. When a response is
already present (`this.#res`) and a new one is assigned, it re-creates the incoming response with a
**mutable** header container and then copies the **existing/old** response headers onto it:

| Header kind | Winner | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `content-type` | **incoming** | old value skipped entirely |
| `set-cookie` | **existing/old** | incoming `Set-Cookie` is **deleted**; only old cookies remain |
| everything else | **existing/old** | old value overwrites incoming value |

So the merge precedence is **old > new**, with two exceptions (`content-type` → new wins;
`set-cookie` → old replaces new instead of merging).

The `Set-Cookie` branch exists because iterating headers collapses multiple cookies into one
comma-joined value; the setter therefore uses `Headers.getSetCookie()` and re-`append`s each cookie
individually (`src/context.ts:421-426`).

---

## 2. Call sites involved

### 2.1 Writers of `c.res` / `context.res`

| Location | Context | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `src/compose.ts:67-69` | Central compose loop | `if (res && (context.finalized === false || isError)) context.res = res` — the main merge trigger for multi-middleware routes |
| `src/hono-base.ts:453` | Single-handler fast path | `c.res = await this.#notFoundHandler(c)` inside the synthetic `next()` callback |
| `src/middleware/compress/index.ts:126` | `compress()` after `next()` | `ctx.res = new Response(ctx.res.body.pipeThrough(stream), ctx.res)` |
| `src/middleware/etag/index.ts:119` | `etag()` 304 path | `c.res = new Response(null, { status: 304, ... })`, then deletes non-retained headers (`:126-130`) |
| `src/middleware/pretty-json/index.ts:64` | `prettyJSON()` after `next()` | re-wraps the body in a new `Response` |
| `src/middleware/trailing-slash/index.ts:71,155` | Redirect after 404 | `c.res = c.redirect(...)` |
| `src/middleware/method-not-allowed/index.ts:137` | 405 response | replaces the 404 response |
| `src/adapter/cloudflare-pages/handler.ts:80` | Pages adapter | `context.res = await executionCtx.next()` (assigns a `fetch` response, i.e. immutable headers) |
| `src/hono.test.ts:1206` | Test-only escape hatch | `c.res = undefined` deliberately clears state before re-assigning |

> `src/http-exception.ts:57` (`this.res = options?.res`) is the `HTTPException` class's own property,
> **not** the `Context` setter. It is unrelated to this merge logic.

### 2.2 Readers / plumbing that interact with the setter

| Location | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/context.ts:403-407` | `get res()` lazily creates `#res` from `#preparedHeaders`, so merely **reading** `c.res` changes whether a later assignment merges |
| `src/context.ts:519-532` | `header()` writes to `#res.headers` if present, else `#preparedHeaders`; when finalized and body unused it re-creates the response (`:520-523`) |
| `src/context.ts:609-657` | `#newResponse()` used by `body/text/json/html/redirect`; clones `#res.headers` (`:614`) and has its own `Set-Cookie`-append rule (`:616-625`) |
| `src/context.ts:288-291` | `createResponseInstance()` — the indirection the setter uses to obtain mutable headers |
| `src/hono-base.ts:480` | Returns `context.res` after compose |
| `src/adapter/aws-lambda/handler.ts:417-430` | Extracts `Set-Cookie` with a `getSetCookie` feature check |
| `src/middleware/secure-headers/secure-headers.ts:232,339` | Mutates `ctx.res.headers` before/after `next()` |
| `src/middleware/logger/index.ts:93`, `cache/index.ts:307-317` | Read/`clone()` the finalized response |

### 2.3 When the merge does *not* run

- The guard is `if (this.#res && _res)` (`src/context.ts:415`). If either side is falsy, the incoming
  value is assigned verbatim.
- `c.res = undefined` resets `#res` and sets `finalized = true` (`:432-433`); the next assignment also
  skips merging (asserted by `src/hono.test.ts:1204-1223`).
- The single-handler fast path returns a handler's `Response` directly
  (`src/hono-base.ts:459-466`) without going through the setter; only the composed path
  (`src/compose.ts:67-69`) and explicit middleware assignments merge.

---

## 3. Current merge order (exact)

```ts
// src/context.ts:414
set res(_res: Response | undefined) {
  if (this.#res && _res) {
    _res = createResponseInstance(_res.body, _res)          // :416  mutable copy, reuses body stream
    for (const [k, v] of this.#res.headers.entries()) {     // :417  iterate OLD headers
      if (k === 'content-type') {                           // :418  content-type: skip
        continue
      }
      if (k === 'set-cookie') {                             // :421  set-cookie: old replaces new
        const cookies = this.#res.headers.getSetCookie()    // :422
        _res.headers.delete('set-cookie')                   // :423  discard ALL incoming cookies
        for (const cookie of cookies) {
          _res.headers.append('set-cookie', cookie)         // :425  re-add old cookies, old order
        }
      } else {
        _res.headers.set(k, v)                              // :428  old value wins
      }
    }
  }
  this.#res = _res                                          // :432
  this.finalized = true                                     // :433
}
```

Step order and semantics:

1. **Re-create the incoming response** with `new Response(_res.body, _res)` (`:416` via
   `:288-291`). This copies status/statusText and puts headers into a fresh, **mutable** `Headers`.
   This is required for `fetch()` responses whose header guard is `immutable`; mutating them directly
   would throw.
2. **Iterate the old headers** in insertion order (`:417`).
3. **`content-type`** → skipped (`:418-420`). The incoming content type survives; the old one is
   discarded. If the incoming response has no content type, the result has none.
4. **`set-cookie`** → `getSetCookie()` on the old headers, `delete('set-cookie')` on the incoming
   response, then `append` each old cookie (`:421-426`). Net effect: **incoming `Set-Cookie` values
   are dropped; the result contains exactly the old cookies in old order.**
5. **All other headers** → `set(k, v)` (`:428`). Old value overwrites any incoming value; incoming
   duplicates are collapsed.
6. Assign `#res` and mark `finalized = true` (`:432-433`), even when `_res` is `undefined`.

Why the `Set-Cookie` special case: `Headers.entries()` exposes multiple `Set-Cookie` values as a
single comma-joined string, and cookie attributes (`Expires=Wed, 21 Oct ...`) contain commas.
Using `set(k, v)` would corrupt cookies, so the code bypasses `v` and uses `getSetCookie()` +
`append()`.

### 3.1 The responder path merges differently

`c.text()/json()/html()/body()` go through `#newResponse` (`src/context.ts:609-657`), which has the
**opposite** precedence:

1. Start from `new Headers(this.#res.headers)` when `#res` exists (`:614`).
2. Apply `arg.headers` (a `Response`/`ResponseInit`): `set-cookie` → `append`, everything else →
   `set` (`:616-625`).
3. Apply the explicit `headers` argument: string → `set`; array → `delete` then `append`
   (`:627-650`).
4. Build the response with the resolved status (`:652-656`).

So for responders **incoming > existing** and cookies **accumulate** (`append`), while for the
`res` setter **existing > incoming** and cookies **replace**. This asymmetry is the core
inconsistency to be aware of when changing behavior.

---

## 4. Existing test coverage

Verified by running the suites locally (see §6). Current state: **green**.

### 4.1 `src/context.test.ts`

| Test | Lines | What it locks in |
|---|---|---|
| `Should append the previous headers to new Response` | 300-311 | old `x-Custom1` survives; incoming `Content-Type` wins |
| `Should return only one content-type value` | 408-418 | responder path content-type override |
| `Should set header values if the #this.headers is set and the arg is ResponseInit` | 420-428 | prepared-header + `ResponseInit` merge |
| `Should set cookie headers when re-assigning Response to c.res` | 430-445 | **incoming cookie dropped**; result length = old length; result equals old cookies |
| `Should keep previous cookies in response headers` | 447-454 | getter + `setCookie()` + `c.json()` retains both cookies |
| `Should set set-cookie header values if c.res is already defined` | 456-466 | responder path preserves `a,b,c` |
| `Should be able to overwrite a fetch response with a new response` | 468-477 | immutable headers re-wrapped; old `X-Custom` carried |
| `Should be able to overwrite a response with a fetch response` | 479-488 | immutable **incoming** response; old `X-Custom` carried |
| `Should be able to set headers if the context is finalized` | 490-495 | `header()` after setter |
| `Should be able to set headers after the response body is consumed` | 497-504 | body-consumed recovery + merge |
| `Should handle headers with array values correctly` | 506-512 | array header append/set |
| `Should remove existing header when new value is empty array` | 514-519 | empty array deletes |
| `Should override the default Content-Type even if the header name casing differs` | 522-527 | case-insensitive content-type |
| `Should apply the last value when header names differ only in casing` | 529-535 | case-insensitive overwrite |
| `c.body() should retain context cookies from context and original response` | 578-592 | context cookies + original-response cookie all present (responder path) |

The immutable-header tests use `makeResponseHeaderImmutable` (`src/context.test.ts:4-36`), which
proxies `headers.set` to throw — this is what forces the setter's defensive re-creation.

### 4.2 `src/hono.test.ts`

| Test | Lines | What it locks in |
|---|---|---|
| `Overwrite the response from middleware after next()` / `Should have the custom header` | 1196-1218 | middleware replacing `c.res` keeps handler's `x-custom` |
| `Should not have the custom header` (`c.res = undefined` first) | 1204-1223 | clearing disables merging |
| `Not Found with a middleware` | 1331-1348 | re-wrap 404 body via `new Response(..., c.res)` |
| `Not Found with some middleware` | 1350-1371 | stacked re-wraps, ordering |
| `Custom 404 Not Found with a middleware like Compress Middleware` | 1389-1407 | `new Response(await c.res.text(), c.res)` |

### 4.3 Other suites

| Test | Lines | What it locks in |
|---|---|---|
| `compose with Context - 401 not authorized` | `src/compose.test.ts:182-200` | middleware assigning `c.res` after `next()` |
| `Multiple values` (cookies) | `src/helper/cookie/index.test.ts:377-391` | multiple `Set-Cookie` rendered as `"a, b"` |
| AWS Lambda `setCookies` | `src/adapter/aws-lambda/handler.ts:417-430` | adapter-level cookie extraction (guarded `getSetCookie`) |

### 4.4 Coverage gaps

- No test asserting that an incoming response's `Set-Cookie` is **merged/appended** — the existing
  test asserts the opposite (`src/context.test.ts:430-445`).
- No test where the **incoming response has no `Content-Type`** while the old one does; current code
  drops the old type (`src/context.ts:418-420`).
- No test mixing multiple old cookies **and** other overriding headers in a single assignment.
- No test for case-insensitive `Set-Cookie` in the setter (relies on `Headers` normalization; the
  literal compare is lowercase at `src/context.ts:421`).
- No test for `getSetCookie` being unavailable: the setter calls it unguarded (`:422`) whereas the
  AWS adapter feature-detects (`src/adapter/aws-lambda/handler.ts:419-421`).
- No test covering "read `c.res` first, then assign" — the getter creates `#res`, which flips the
  merge on (`src/context.ts:403-407` + `:415`).
- No adapter-level test that exercises the setter merge before serialization.

---

## 5. Risks of changing the behavior

1. **Header precedence inversion breaks middleware header preservation.**
   The "old wins" rule is what keeps headers set before/around a handler when a middleware replaces
   the response. Tests `src/context.test.ts:300-311`, `468-488`, `490-504` and
   `src/hono.test.ts:1196-1218` depend on it. Switching to "new wins" would silently drop headers
   from `powered-by`, `secure-headers` (`src/middleware/secure-headers/secure-headers.ts:339`), CORS,
   etc.

2. **Changing `Set-Cookie` from "replace" to "merge" breaks an explicit contract.**
   `src/context.test.ts:430-445` asserts the incoming cookie is discarded and the result equals the
   old cookies. Any merge change must update that test and define duplicate-name/order semantics.

3. **Cookie ordering and duplicate-name precedence are observable.**
   If incoming cookies are kept, you must decide whether they go before or after old ones. Browsers
   resolve duplicate cookie names by last-wins, so order changes which value the client stores. A
   naive `append` can also create duplicate `Set-Cookie` names, inflating headers and changing auth.

4. **Security/statefulness: resurrecting or losing cookies.**
   - Merging could **re-introduce cookies** that a replaced response (e.g. a 304 or redirect built in
     `src/middleware/etag/index.ts:119-130`, `src/middleware/trailing-slash/index.ts:71`) was meant
     to retire.
   - Keeping "replace" can **silently lose a handler's `Set-Cookie`** if a middleware touched `c.res`
     before the handler response was assigned. This is the current, arguably surprising, behavior.
   Document the chosen semantics explicitly.

5. **`content-type` handling is fragile.**
   The skip at `src/context.ts:418-420` means incoming always wins, but if the incoming response has
   no content type, the merged response has none. "Fixing" it by falling back to the old type can
   serve a stale `application/json` for an HTML/redirect body. Add explicit tests before changing.

6. **Immutable-header handling must remain.**
   `createResponseInstance(_res.body, _res)` (`:416`) exists so `fetch()`/immutable responses can be
   mutated. Refactoring to mutate `_res.headers` directly will throw (`TypeError: immutable`) and
   break `src/context.test.ts:468-495`. A refactor must re-create the `Response` (or clone headers).

7. **Body stream lifetime.**
   The re-creation reuses `_res.body` (`:416`). If the body is already consumed/disturbed, this can
   throw; middleware such as `etag`/`pretty-json` explicitly cancel/consume first
   (`src/middleware/etag/index.ts:118`, `src/middleware/pretty-json/index.ts:63`). Reordering or
   double-cloning could break these.

8. **`finalized` and the `undefined` escape hatch.**
   The setter always sets `finalized = true`, including `c.res = undefined` (`:432-433`). The
   single-handler return path (`src/hono-base.ts:459-466`) and `compose.ts:67-69` both branch on
   `finalized`; changing when it flips can turn a valid 404 into the "Context is not finalized"
   error (`src/hono-base.ts:474-478`) or vice versa.

9. **Read-before-write makes behavior path-dependent.**
   Because the getter lazily materializes `#res` (`:403-407`), whether a merge occurs depends on
   whether any code read `c.res` earlier. Any change that removes the getter side effect (or makes
   the setter unconditional) will change behavior for routes that only *read* headers.

10. **Runtime compatibility.**
    `getSetCookie()` is assumed present in the setter (`:422`) but guarded elsewhere
    (`src/adapter/aws-lambda/handler.ts:419-421`). Extending reliance on it risks breaking older
    Node/edge runtimes; a guard or a fallback is advisable.

11. **Performance on the hot path.**
    Every composed response assignment re-creates a `Response` + `Headers` and iterates all old
    headers. Making the merge more elaborate (dedupe, sort, re-clone) adds per-request work; this
    repo maintains benchmark/perf harnesses (`benchmarks/`, `perf-measures/`), so changes should be
    measured.

12. **Mutation-during-iteration.**
    The loop iterates `this.#res.headers` while mutating `_res.headers` — two distinct objects, so it
    is safe. A refactor that iterates the target headers while appending/deleting could skip or
    duplicate entries.

---

## 6. Verification performed

All commands were read-only and executed from the repo root:

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/context.test.ts --project main --reporter=dot
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       63 passed (63)
# context.ts coverage: 94.49% stmts, 100% branches

$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/hono.test.ts src/helper/cookie/index.test.ts src/compose.test.ts --project main --reporter=dot
Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       287 passed (287)
```

No `git add`/`git commit` was run; the only new file is this `INVESTIGATION.md`.

---

## 7. Recommendation for a future change

Before altering the merge order, lock the intended contract with tests:

1. Add a test for the desired `Set-Cookie` semantics when both old and new responses carry cookies
   (merge vs replace, ordering, duplicate names).
2. Add the missing `Content-Type`-absent case.
3. Add a feature-absence case for `getSetCookie` if runtime support is not guaranteed.
4. Keep the immutable-response re-wrap (`createResponseInstance`) and body-stream handling intact.
5. Update `src/context.test.ts:430-445` and the `hono.test.ts` middleware-overwrite cases together
   with any semantic change, and re-run the adapter suites (`src/adapter/aws-lambda`,
   `adapters/aws-lambda`, `adapters/lambda-edge`) that serialize `Set-Cookie`.

| `src/middleware/secure-headers/secure-headers.ts:232,339` | Mutates `ctx.res.headers` before/after `next()` |
| `src/middleware/logger/index.ts:93`, `cache/index.ts:307-317` | Read/`clone()` the finalized response |

### 2.3 When the merge does *not* run

- The guard is `if (this.#res && _res)` (`src/context.ts:415`). If either side is falsy, the incoming
  value is assigned verbatim.
- `c.res = undefined` resets `#res` and sets `finalized = true` (`:432-433`); the next assignment also
  skips merging (asserted by `src/hono.test.ts:1204-1223`).
- The single-handler fast path returns a handler's `Response` directly
  (`src/hono-base.ts:459-466`) without going through the setter; only the composed path
  (`src/compose.ts:67-69`) and explicit middleware assignments merge.

## 3. Current merge order (exact)

```ts
// src/context.ts:414
set res(_res: Response | undefined) {
  if (this.#res && _res) {
    _res = createResponseInstance(_res.body, _res)          // :416  mutable copy, reuses body stream
    for (const [k, v] of this.#res.headers.entries()) {     // :417  iterate OLD headers
      if (k === 'content-type') {                           // :418  content-type: skip
        continue
      }
      if (k === 'set-cookie') {                             // :421  set-cookie: old replaces new
        const cookies = this.#res.headers.getSetCookie()    // :422
        _res.headers.delete('set-cookie')                   // :423  discard ALL incoming cookies
        for (const cookie of cookies) {
          _res.headers.append('set-cookie', cookie)         // :425  re-add old cookies, old order
        }
      } else {
        _res.headers.set(k, v)                              // :428  old value wins
      }
    }
  }
  this.#res = _res                                          // :432
  this.finalized = true                                     // :433
}
```

Step order and semantics:

1. **Re-create the incoming response** with `new Response(_res.body, _res)` (`:416` via
   `:288-291`). This copies status/statusText and puts headers into a fresh, **mutable** `Headers`.
   This is required for `fetch()` responses whose header guard is `immutable`; mutating them directly
   would throw.
2. **Iterate the old headers** in insertion order (`:417`).
3. **`content-type`** → skipped (`:418-420`). The incoming content type survives; the old one is
   discarded. If the incoming response has no content type, the result has none.
4. **`set-cookie`** → `getSetCookie()` on the old headers, `delete('set-cookie')` on the incoming
   response, then `append` each old cookie (`:421-426`). Net effect: **incoming `Set-Cookie` values
   are dropped; the result contains exactly the old cookies in old order.**
5. **All other headers** → `set(k, v)` (`:428`). Old value overwrites any incoming value; incoming
   duplicates are collapsed.
6. Assign `#res` and mark `finalized = true` (`:432-433`), even when `_res` is `undefined`.

Why the `Set-Cookie` special case: `Headers.entries()` exposes multiple `Set-Cookie` values as a
single comma-joined string, and cookie attributes (`Expires=Wed, 21 Oct ...`) contain commas.
Using `set(k, v)` would corrupt cookies, so the code bypasses `v` and uses `getSetCookie()` +
`append()`.

### 3.1 The responder path merges differently

`c.text()/json()/html()/body()` go through `#newResponse` (`src/context.ts:609-657`), which has the
**opposite** precedence:

1. Start from `new Headers(this.#res.headers)` when `#res` exists (`:614`).
2. Apply `arg.headers` (a `Response`/`ResponseInit`): `set-cookie` → `append`, everything else →
   `set` (`:616-625`).
3. Apply the explicit `headers` argument: string → `set`; array → `delete` then `append`
   (`:627-650`).
4. Build the response with the resolved status (`:652-656`).

So for responders **incoming > existing** and cookies **accumulate** (`append`), while for the
`res` setter **existing > incoming** and cookies **replace**. This asymmetry is the core
inconsistency to be aware of when changing behavior.

## 5. Risks of changing the behavior

1. **Header precedence inversion breaks middleware header preservation.**
   The "old wins" rule is what keeps headers set before/around a handler when a middleware replaces
   the response. Tests `src/context.test.ts:300-311`, `468-488`, `490-504` and
   `src/hono.test.ts:1196-1218` depend on it. Switching to "new wins" would silently drop headers
   from `powered-by`, `secure-headers` (`src/middleware/secure-headers/secure-headers.ts:339`), CORS,
   etc.

2. **Changing `Set-Cookie` from "replace" to "merge" breaks an explicit contract.**
   `src/context.test.ts:430-445` asserts the incoming cookie is discarded and the result equals the
   old cookies. Any merge change must update that test and define duplicate-name/order semantics.

3. **Cookie ordering and duplicate-name precedence are observable.**
   If incoming cookies are kept, you must decide whether they go before or after old ones. Browsers
   resolve duplicate cookie names by last-wins, so order changes which value the client stores. A
   naive `append` can also create duplicate `Set-Cookie` names, inflating headers and changing auth.

4. **Security/statefulness: resurrecting or losing cookies.**
   - Merging could **re-introduce cookies** that a replaced response (e.g. a 304 or redirect built in
     `src/middleware/etag/index.ts:119-130`, `src/middleware/trailing-slash/index.ts:71`) was meant
     to retire.
   - Keeping "replace" can **silently lose a handler's `Set-Cookie`** if a middleware touched `c.res`
     before the handler response was assigned. This is the current, arguably surprising, behavior.
   Document the chosen semantics explicitly.

5. **`content-type` handling is fragile.**
   The skip at `src/context.ts:418-420` means incoming always wins, but if the incoming response has
   no content type, the merged response has none. "Fixing" it by falling back to the old type can
   serve a stale `application/json` for an HTML/redirect body. Add explicit tests before changing.

6. **Immutable-header handling must remain.**
   `createResponseInstance(_res.body, _res)` (`:416`) exists so `fetch()`/immutable responses can be
   mutated. Refactoring to mutate `_res.headers` directly will throw (`TypeError: immutable`) and
   break `src/context.test.ts:468-495`. A refactor must re-create the `Response` (or clone headers).

7. **Body stream lifetime.**
   The re-creation reuses `_res.body` (`:416`). If the body is already consumed/disturbed, this can
   throw; middleware such as `etag`/`pretty-json` explicitly cancel/consume first
   (`src/middleware/etag/index.ts:118`, `src/middleware/pretty-json/index.ts:63`). Reordering or
   double-cloning could break these.

8. **`finalized` and the `undefined` escape hatch.**
   The setter always sets `finalized = true`, including `c.res = undefined` (`:432-433`). The
   single-handler return path (`src/hono-base.ts:459-466`) and `compose.ts:67-69` both branch on
   `finalized`; changing when it flips can turn a valid 404 into the "Context is not finalized"
   error (`src/hono-base.ts:474-478`) or vice versa.

9. **Read-before-write makes behavior path-dependent.**
   Because the getter lazily materializes `#res` (`:403-407`), whether a merge occurs depends on
   whether any code read `c.res` earlier. Any change that removes the getter side effect (or makes
   the setter unconditional) will change behavior for routes that only *read* headers.

10. **Runtime compatibility.**
    `getSetCookie()` is assumed present in the setter (`:422`) but guarded elsewhere
    (`src/adapter/aws-lambda/handler.ts:419-421`). Extending reliance on it risks breaking older
    Node/edge runtimes; a guard or a fallback is advisable.

11. **Performance on the hot path.**
    Every composed response assignment re-creates a `Response` + `Headers` and iterates all old
    headers. Making the merge more elaborate (dedupe, sort, re-clone) adds per-request work; this
    repo maintains benchmark/perf harnesses (`benchmarks/`, `perf-measures/`), so changes should be
    measured.

12. **Mutation-during-iteration.**
    The loop iterates `this.#res.headers` while mutating `_res.headers` — two distinct objects, so it
    is safe. A refactor that iterates the target headers while appending/deleting could skip or
    duplicate entries.
